correctness.rationale: The fixed-point criterion for 0,1,2 is derived directly from the stable ranks. The sole-2 deletion splits an at-most-one equal pair, and endpoint cases give exactly A_m, B_m as fixed-point-free candidates for every m≥2. Exact Hamming counts leave A_m only for even m. Its stable π is conjugate over the arbitrary odd ring Z/(2m+1) to multiplication by the inverse of 2 with zero spliced into one orbit; transitivity forces the modulus prime and 2 primitive. A standalone enumerator independently checks all length cases at m=2..10 and two-word/modular identities through m=100. Finite checks are not the infinite proof; symbolic steps establish the universal statement.

originality.rationale: Kumallagov 2026 proves one sufficient prime-root family, not the necessary-and-sufficient arithmetic criterion and uniqueness for all (m,m,1) sharp images. Fici et al. 2025 covers unrestricted ternary existence and a different periodic construction, not this criterion. Available finite counts do not imply the all-parameter statement. value.rationale: Completes the naturally posed sharp Parikh-vector existence question for an infinite balanced singleton-content family, including exact 0/1 counts and uniqueness. It explains the persistence of an arithmetic primitive-root obstruction after moving from binary to ternary with only one third-symbol occurrence, despite unconditional unrestricted ternary existence. The two-candidate fixed-point-free lemma is an independent structural classification rather than a trivial finite extension.
